Sample.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/3] The data were analyzed using an intent-to-treat approach, defined as "the inclusion of all eligible patients regardless of compliance with the protocol."50 Therefore, the 107 subjects randomized into the protocol were included, and follow-up continued even for those subjects who left the protocol to preserve, as much as possible, the effects of initial randomization.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/13] To examine the efficacy of different psychotherapeutic approaches, we compared individual CBT and family treatment approaches to adolescent depression with nondirective supportive therapy (NST) as a third cell to control for the nonspecific effects of psychotherapy. We hypothesized that at the end of treatment, patients treated with CBT or family therapy would show more rapid improvement and be more likely to achieve clinical remission than those treated with supportive therapy for depression, suicidality, and functional impairment, because CBT and family therapy specifically target factors associated with the onset, persistence, and recurrence of depression.
dxgive.warning: No explicit mention of formal diagnostic criteria for inclusion; entry appears symptom-based.
